lines: From Personnel, select Manage Invites.
The Invites page separates the invitation history from the Send Invites form.
Its history has Email Address, Sent On and Completed On columns.
This walkthrough invites a fictional new member, Derrick Gibson, and
verifies the result from both sides.
An invitation is useful when a new team member should complete
their own account details instead of an administrator entering every
credential through Add a Person.
Enter the intended recipient in Email Addresses.
The help explains that multiple addresses can be separated by commas.
This exercise uses a single fictional training address.
Review the destination and select Send Invites.
The saved row then shows the address, a Sent On time and
Pending under Completed On.
Check that row for the intended recipient.
Pending is an invitation state; it does not establish that the recipient
has finished joining the department.
While the invitation is pending, the row offers Resend Invite.
If delivery needs another attempt, review the intended address
and confirm that the recipient actually receives the invitation.
Here the controlled local Mailpit inbox contains the Resgrid invitation
for the training department.
Opening that email shows the inviting administrator, the department
and a Set up account button.
This mailbox is our local recording tool; your members use their own mailbox.
Follow Set up account to the registration form.
The invitation link itself is private and is not shown in this lesson.
The form identifies the department the recipient is joining.
Enter the member’s own name, a unique Username, and matching password fields.
Our fictional example is Derrick Gibson, and the passwords remain masked.
The displayed password requirement is at least eight characters,
including a digit, an uppercase letter and a lowercase letter.
Review the terms of use and privacy policy notice before Register, because
signing up accepts those terms.
The notice also describes existing-account linking, but this
exercise creates a new fictional account.
Select Register after that review.
The returned workspace is signed in as Derrick Gibson.
Check the name at the upper left and the intended department in the header.
That visible signed-in result is stronger evidence than assuming
the Register button worked.
The new member now has a department workspace in this local exercise.
Operational status and staffing controls are separate from accepting
the invitation; no responding status or staffing change is performed here.
Return to Manage Invites under the administrator account.
The same recipient now has an actual Completed On date
and time rather than Pending.
Sent On remains a separate value.
Compare those two columns when checking whether an invitation
was merely sent or was completed.
In this recorded example, completion is saved at seventeen fifteen and
fifty-six seconds on the displayed date.
This administrative readback confirms the completed invitation independently
of the member’s signed-in page.
Open Personnel and use Search to find Derrick Gibson.
The saved row shows Normal under State, Available under Staffing
and Standing By under Status.
Roles is still blank for this newly invited member.
Review the department group and operational role the person needs as
part of your own onboarding process.
The member-access walkthrough demonstrates those separate controls.
This invitation exercise verifies membership without granting a
department administrator role or assigning an operational role.
Use the same invitation and verification process for community paramedicine
and mental health response teams, search-and-rescue organizations, security
departments, wildland contractors and industrial emergency teams, as
well as fire and E M S departments.
Send to the intended recipient, verify delivery, let the member complete
the form, and check the completed invitation and personnel row.
Those readbacks help administrators distinguish an outstanding invitation
from a member who has actually joined.
